maria: quick heads-up: after merging the AWQ packing refactor I'm seeing 99p latency spikes on some short-convo workloads. baseline p99 jumped from ~45ms -> ~120ms. anyone else?
lee: yep saw that on last night's nightly perf run. tracer shows kernel-selection thrash in attention for seq_len<=64. looks like pack serialization cost dominating. :thinking_face:
sachin: do you have perf traces? sounds like KV cache serialization causing CPU STALLs while waiting on GPU kernel selection.
maria: attaching perf dump snippet from perf-bot:```
perf top -p 1234
 23.5%  runtime::pack_serialize
 17.1%  kernel_selector::choose_kernel
  9.3%  kv_cache::copy_prefix
  6.0%  cuda_memcpy_async
```
lee: interesting — choose_kernel being expensive suggests we compute heuristics per-request. memoizing kernel choices keyed on (model_variant, seq_len_bucket, batch_size, group_size) should help.
sachin: memoize + warm cache should help, yes. but pack_serialize is still heavy. are we running group_size=64? AWQ with group_size=64 packs a lot of tiny tensors, causing many memcpy ops and syscalls.
maria: test config i ran: AWQ, group_size=64, pack_mode=serial, batch_size=1, kv_cache enabled. when i switch to group_size=32 and pack_mode=parallel, p99 drops back to ~48ms.
lee: we should add a rule in KernelChooser: if seq_len < 80 && kv_cache_active && batch_size <= 4 => prefer the `kv-optimized` kernel (fewer mem copies) even if reported FLOPS lower. add unit test + perf guardrail. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: nightly perf test: branch int8-awq-serialize-fix reduced p99 by 38% on short-convo-stress.
sachin: one open question: what's the calibration effect here? previously enabling calibration/bias-correction increased inference CPU by ~5-7% but reduced output shift; is that acceptable?
maria: calibration is offline, but we currently apply per-group correction at runtime when loading weight-only AWQ checkpoints — that runtime per-load correction is the culprit. moving correction entirely to load-time (precompute corrections into packed weights) should remove the runtime cost.
lee: plan: 1) move bias-correction to load-time; 2) memoize kernel choices with a small TTL keyed by (model, seq_bucket, batch, group_size); 3) default pack_mode=parallel for small batch sizes; 4) add a short-convo perf test in CI that exercises seq_len buckets under 80.
maria: i'll open the PR with tests. assigning @sachin for perf validation and @lee for kernel-chooser changes. including a quick perf script i used:```
// run_short_convo.sh
for gs in 32 48 64; do
  RD_DEBUG_PACK_MODE=parallel ./bench --model gpt-large --batch 1 --seq 40 --group_size $gs --quant awq
done
```
lee: :thumbsup:
sachin: another idea — emit a lightweight histogram telemetry for seq_len distribution and pack_serialization_ms to console so routing can pick regionally optimized kernels automatically.
maria: good call. i'll add telemetry event `pack_serialization_ms` tagged by model, group_size, pack_mode.
perf-bot: deployed perf alert rule: pack_serialization_ms > 20ms for 5% of requests -> page eng-runtime on-call.
maria: thanks all — i'll kick off the branch and post the PR link when ready.
